However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), and PGS000788’s construction is a re-weighted variant of PGS000077 (inverse weights), creating unresolved ambiguity about which weighting is intrinsically better for standalone PRS use; additionally, several competing CLL-focused scores show strong ORs but target a narrower subtype than the generic target trait.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305), but most report only full-model discrimination (not PRS-only), making cross-model comparison suboptimal per the provided domain guidance. Among the direct lymphoid-leukemia–EFO models, PGS000788 has coherent endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and the strongest visible effect-size evidence (HR per SD=1.7, 95% CI 1.53–1.88) with a large European evaluation sample (n=391,338). Its higher full-model AUROC/C-index (0.738/0.756) is supportive but discounted because it is not PRS-only, and its construction note (“inverse variant weights” from PGS000077) raises some uncertainty about implementation details and comparability. Because no candidate provides clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R² and several near-synonymous direct matches exist, confidence is moderate rather than high.

All 13 candidates are direct matches at the broad disease-family level, but several are for the chronic lymphocytic leukemia subtype (PGS000646/647/648/649/650/651/874/003453) rather than generic lymphoid leukemia; given the domain note that acute vs chronic distinctions are material, these are not clearly the best match for a generic “lymphoid leukemia” target. Among the models explicitly mapped to lymphoid leukemia (PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305), PGS000788 has coherent endpoint fidelity (“Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia”), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), a sizable variant set (75), and the strongest visible per-SD effect size (HR=1.7, 95% CI 1.53–1.88) alongside the highest reported full-model AUROC/C-index (0.738/0.756) in EUR evaluation. Limitation: the key performance figures are full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), and PGS000788 is described as an inverse-weight reparameterization of PGS000077 rather than an independently derived score, so superiority vs PGS000077 (very similar endpoint/covariates/variants, HR=1.45) is not decisively established from PRS-comparable metrics—hence only moderate confidence and a sub-optimal direct-match designation.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with some using the closely related M81 (osteoporosis without pathological fracture) endpoint. Among the set, PGS005155 is best supported structurally because it uses PRS-CSx (a cross-ancestry joint modeling shrinkage approach) with a genome-wide variant count (908,465) and is evaluated in an East Asian cohort (n=58,611), which is more informative than sparse framework scores and more methodologically robust than the other non-PRS-CSx options shown. The main limitation is that most candidates (including PGS005155) lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) and provide only an effect-size beta without clear interpretability for discrimination; this makes the choice less definitive, keeping confidence moderate and the overall outcome sub-optimal despite a clear direct match.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis at the trait level, but their evidence quality is mixed. Two candidates (PGS001273/PGS001274) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as systematically underperforming disease-focused models; their attractive full-model AUROC (~0.79) is also accompanied by small PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.57; PGS-only R2 ~0.007–0.009), suggesting the high AUROC is largely covariate-driven. Several newer 2024 models (PGS004495/PGS004565 etc.) have unknown covariates and only modest per-SD ORs (~1.18–1.33) with no PRS-only AUC/R2, limiting comparability. Among the remaining genome-wide shrinkage options with explicit effect-size evidence, PGS005155 (PRS-CSx; GWAS EAS+EUR; EVAL EAS) is methodologically strong (cross-ancestry shrinkage) and shows the largest reported effect size in its family (β=1.144 vs β=1.094 for PGS005146), making it the best-supported single choice from the visible metadata. Main limitation: performance reporting is not standardized across candidates (β vs OR vs PRS-only AUC/R2), and several models lack PRS-comparable metrics, so the preference cannot be made with high certainty.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis at the concept level, but most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (AUC/R2) and several come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., PGS001273/PGS001274 from the “813 traits” framework; PGS001883/PGS002095 from the “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” framework), which domain guidance treats as systematically weaker when better-designed disease-focused alternatives exist. Among the non-framework, endpoint-aligned options, PGS005155 (PRS-CSx) is methodologically strong (cross-ancestry shrinkage/transfer; large genome-wide variant count 908,465), is directly phenotyped as osteoporosis, and has East Asian evaluation with an explicit effect-size signal (β=1.1443), making it the best-supported single choice from the visible evidence. Limitation: effect-size reporting is not directly comparable across the pool (several models report OR per SD or only incremental R2), many candidates have missing PRS-only AUC/R2, and there is no single clearly dominant, cleanly comparable performance metric across candidates—so the recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis by trait_reported/trait_efo, with some being narrower ICD10 M81 (osteoporosis without pathological fracture) or time-to-event variants. Among the set, PGS005155 (PRS-CSx) has strong methodological support (cross-ancestry joint modeling; genome-wide shrinkage with ~908k variants) and clean, basic covariates (age, sex), and it is evaluated in an East Asian cohort, which is explicit transportability evidence rather than a pan-trait framework artifact. However, the pool lacks a clearly dominant, directly comparable PRS-only discrimination metric across most models: many newer genome-wide models report only effect sizes (often without CIs) or incremental R2, while the only explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 come from the snpnet pan-trait framework models (PGS001273/PGS001274), which domain guidance flags as prone to over-selection despite complete metrics. Because the best-supported choice rests mainly on structural/method evidence and limited effect-size reporting (β given, not OR/AUC/R2), confidence is moderate and the overall outcome remains sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but they differ in endpoint specificity and evidentiary completeness. The snpnet UKB pan-trait framework scores (PGS001273/PGS001274) provide explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2, yet domain_knowledge cautions that such framework-derived sparse models often generalize poorly and that full-model AUROC can be largely covariate-driven (consistent here: high full-model AUROC with small incremental AUROC and low PGS-only R2). Several newer disease-focused candidates provide only effect sizes without PRS-only discrimination metrics; among those, PGS005155 (PRS-CSx) has methodologically strong cross-ancestry joint modeling (EUR+EAS GWAS, EAS evaluation) and is the strongest within its study family versus the single-ancestry PRS-CS alternative (PGS005146) based on the larger reported effect (β=1.144 vs 1.094). Main limitation: key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are missing for most non-framework candidates, and PGS005155’s evaluation is EAS-only, so without a specified deployment ancestry and without comparable discrimination metrics across the pool, the choice cannot be rated as clearly high-quality.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, with some being ICD subtype variants (M81) or time-to-event; none shows explicit non-comparable clinical risk-calculator packaging. The strongest structural methods in this pool are genome-wide Bayesian shrinkage/cross-ancestry extensions (PRS-CS / PRS-CSx) versus pan-trait sparse snpnet (PGS001273/PGS001274) and portability/penalized-regression scores with weak partial-r (PGS001883/PGS002095). PGS005155 (PRS-CSx) is preferred because it is a modern cross-ancestry joint model (EAS+EUR GWAS; EAS evaluation) with very high variant count (908,465), which domain guidance ranks as a strong methodological signal for generalizable PRS compared with sparse framework scores and partial-correlation portability sweeps. However, confidence is limited because most candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/R2) and several alternatives report only single effect sizes (often without CI), making it hard to establish a clearly best-performing model from visible evidence alone.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (osteoporosis) based on trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, with some endpoint variants (e.g., M81 without pathological fracture; time-to-event). The strongest method-family signal among the set is PRS-CSx (PGS005155), a cross-ancestry extension of genome-wide Bayesian shrinkage, evaluated in an East Asian cohort (n=58,611) with basic covariates (age, sex) and a reported effect size (β=1.1443) that is larger than the sibling EAS-only PRS-CS model (PGS005146; β=1.0937). Many other models either come from known pan-trait/portability framework papers (e.g., snpnet ‘813 traits’ and ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores’) or lack PRS-comparable performance metrics, and the Commun Biol 2024 family reports only modest ORs with unknown covariates. Main limitation: key metrics are heterogeneous and often missing (no PRS-only AUROC/R² for most), and PGS005155’s evidence is effect-size-only with East-Asian-only evaluation, making cross-candidate comparability and general deployment strength uncertain; thus the direct-match recommendation is present but not high-confidence.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis by trait_reported/trait_efo, but the evidence is heterogeneous and often incomplete. The snpnet pan-trait framework models (PGS001273/PGS001274) report explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2, but domain guidance warns these UKB-wide framework sparse models commonly generalize poorly; their very high full-model AUROC with small incremental AUROC/low PGS-only R2 suggests covariate-driven discrimination. Among the non-framework candidates, the strongest structural signal is method: multi-score aggregation is strongly preferred, and PGS004810 (PRSmixPlus) is an ensemble-style method with very high variant count (1,876,917) and reports an incremental R2 (0.022) in European evaluation. Competing disease-focused/benchmarking candidates mostly lack PRS-comparable metrics and/or provide only moderate effect sizes (e.g., OR~1.31 for PGS002768) or unknown covariates (PGS004495/PGS004565). Because PGS004810’s evidence is limited to incremental R2 (no PGS-only AUROC/R2) and it is evaluated only in EUR with a modest validation size, the selection remains weakly supported, hence sub-optimal outcome and low confidence.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait osteoporosis by trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, but the evidence does not clearly single out a best model. Pan-trait/portability framework scores (PGS001273/PGS001274 from the “813 traits” UKB sweep; PGS001883/PGS002095 from the “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” sweep) have explicit PRS-only metrics but are penalized by the domain guidance as framework-derived and typically less reliable for external performance. Among the non-framework options, the 2024 Commun Biol cluster (PGS004490/PGS004495/PGS004560/PGS004565) is endpoint-aligned and uses methodologically strong approaches (LDpred2 and an ensemble-like RFDiseasemetaPRS) with genome-wide variant counts (~1.06M), which is supportive structurally; within that cluster, PGS004565 has the strongest reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.328222) versus its siblings (e.g., OR=1.320825 for PGS004560; OR~1.20 for LDpred2 versions), making it the best-supported pick on available comparable performance evidence. Main limitation: for these 2024 models, covariates are ‘Unknown’ and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the apparent advantage relies on a single effect-size field and remains insufficient for a high-confidence choice; additionally, other direct-match options exist with different ancestry focus (e.g., EAS-only PGS005146/PGS005155) and different metric types (e.g., incremental R² for PGS004810), making cross-model comparability limited from the visible metadata alone.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with some subtype variants (M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture) and one time-to-event endpoint. The strongest structural-method candidate in the set is PGS004810 (PRSmixPlus; 1,876,917 variants), which aligns exactly to osteoporosis and uses a method family characterized as integrative/multi-component (a top positive signal in the provided domain guidance) with basic demographic/PC covariates. However, the pool lacks a clearly decisive, PRS-comparable performance metric across the top modern candidates: PGS004810 reports only incremental R2 (0.022) and not PRS-only AUROC/R2; several other genome-wide models report only OR/beta without clear per-SD specification, limiting comparability. While older framework scores (PGS001273/PGS001274) do report PRS-only AUROC/R2, they come from a pan-trait UKB framework that the domain guidance flags as systematically weaker for external generalization, so they are not preferred despite better-exposed PRS-only metrics. Overall, PGS004810 is best supported on endpoint fidelity + method/variant-count signals, but missing PRS-comparable performance reporting keeps confidence and outcome sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

All listed candidates are direct matches for the target trait (testicular carcinoma) with coherent endpoint fields (e.g., trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are malignant neoplasm of testis or testicular cancer). Within the large same-family cluster from Cancer PRSweb (Am J Hum Genet, 2020-12-15) with comparable basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4) and European evaluation, PGS000604 is best supported because it shows the strongest reported effect size (OR=2.106 per SD, CI 1.729–2.565) and among the top full-model discrimination metrics in that family (AUROC=0.703; Nagelkerke R²=0.0882) with a larger UKB-based training/validation context than many siblings. Remaining limitation: performance evidence is primarily full-model (covariate-adjusted) rather than explicitly PRS-only, and an alternative from a different study (PGS000796, Nat Commun) reports higher full-model AUROC but uses a reweighted prior score with non-comparable R² reporting (very high R²=0.605) and different endpoint framing (incident cancer/time-to-event), making cross-study metric comparisons less reliable; therefore confidence is not high.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target disease concept (testicular carcinoma / malignant neoplasm of testis / testicular cancer), with generally coherent endpoint fields. Among the Cancer PRSweb sibling models (PGS000595–PGS000604) that share very similar phenotyping and basic covariates (age, sex, batch/array, PCs), PGS000604 is best supported by the visible evidence: it has the highest reported AUROC within that coherent family (0.703, European evaluation), the highest reported pseudo-R² in that family (0.0882), and a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=2.106) than its closest sibling (PGS000602: AUROC=0.698, pseudo-R²=0.0839, OR=2.055). While PGS000796 and PGS001164 report much higher full-model AUROC values, they come from different study archetypes with less directly comparable performance reporting (and for PGS000796 the very large R²/full-model discrimination is not interpretable as PRS-only from the provided metadata; for PGS001164 the study is a pan-trait UKB framework where domain guidance warns against over-ranking based on exposed PRS-only metrics alone when coherent disease-focused candidates exist). Main limitation: across all models, truly PRS-only comparable metrics are mostly absent (many AUROCs appear to be full-model with covariates), so the preference for PGS000604 rests on within-family consistency rather than a clean cross-study PRS-only comparison.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (testicular carcinoma) with endpoint-consistent phenotyping (e.g., “Malignant neoplasm of testis” / “Testicular cancer”, including one explicitly incident endpoint). Within the coherent Cancer PRSweb near-clone family (PGS000595–PGS000604), PGS000604 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has the strongest reported discrimination/effect evidence among those siblings (full-model AUROC 0.703 with basic covariates; OR per SD 2.106 [1.729–2.565]; highest pseudo-R² 0.0882) with matched European evaluation and no heavy clinical covariate packaging. The main limitation is that most candidates (including PGS000604) report primarily full-model metrics rather than clearly isolated PRS-only metrics, and there is a competing, differently sourced model (PGS000796) with much higher full-model AUROC but unclear PRS-only contribution and a method description suggesting score repackaging; this keeps confidence at Moderate rather than High.

All listed candidates are direct matches for testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (e.g., “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Incident testicular cancer”) and broadly comparable basic covariates. Within the coherent Cancer PRSweb sibling set (PGS000595–PGS000604) that shares the same endpoint/covariates and European evaluation, PGS000604 is best supported by the strongest reported validation package among siblings: highest full-model AUROC (0.703, 95% CI 0.659–0.745), highest Nagelkerke’s pseudo-R² (0.0882), and strongest per-SD OR (2.106, 95% CI 1.729–2.565), with larger validation (n=1,484) than most siblings. Limitation: key metrics are full-model (age/sex/PC-adjusted) rather than explicit PGS-only discrimination, and a separate non-sibling candidate (PGS000796) reports a much higher full-model AUROC but is a cross-cancer risk-factor–integrated package with non-comparable reporting (and unclear PRS-only contribution), so confidence is moderated despite a clear within-family winner.

All listed candidates are direct matches to testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. Among the coherent Cancer PRSweb sibling set (PGS000595–PGS000604) with the same endpoint (“Malignant neoplasm of testis”), basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs), and EUR evaluation, PGS000604 shows the strongest reported validation performance (full-model AUROC 0.703 with Nagelkerke R² 0.0882 and OR per SD 2.106 [1.729–2.565]) and uses more variants than the closely competing UKB-trained sibling PGS000602 (44 vs 40) with slightly weaker metrics (AUROC 0.698; R² 0.0839; OR 2.055). While PGS000796 and PGS001164 report higher full-model AUROC, their study archetypes (pan-cancer integration / pan-trait sparse framework) and/or reliance on full-model metrics make cross-model comparison less reliable per the provided domain guidance; thus the best-supported choice from the most coherent direct-match family is PGS000604. Main limitation: all top candidates primarily report full-model discrimination (limited PRS-only metrics), so confidence is moderated by comparability constraints.

All listed candidates are direct matches for testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer, with phenotype-aligned endpoints (mostly “Malignant neoplasm of testis”; one “Incident testicular cancer”). Within the coherent Cancer PRSweb sibling cluster (PGS000595–PGS000604) that shares the same phenotype and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array/batch), PGS000604 is best supported by having the strongest reported validation discrimination and effect sizes in that family (full-model AUROC 0.703 with OR per SD 2.106) and higher explained variance (Nagelkerke’s pseudo-R² 0.0882) versus close sibling PGS000602 (AUROC 0.698; OR 2.055). The main limitation is that the reported AUROCs are full-model (covariate-adjusted) rather than explicitly PRS-only metrics, and a competing direct-match model (PGS000796) reports higher full-model AUROC/C-index in a large evaluation but uses a derivative/reweighted score with unclear comparability of its high R² reporting, making the best choice not completely unambiguous from visible metadata alone.

All listed candidates are direct matches to testicular carcinoma/testis malignancy by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus the most comparable performance evidence and method within this direct-match set. Among the coherent Cancer PRSweb sibling models (PGS000595–PGS000604) with similar endpoints and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch/array), PGS000604 (P+T, 44 variants; UKB-trained) shows the strongest validation evidence in this family: highest full-model AUROC (0.703, 95% CI 0.659–0.745), highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0882), and strong per-SD OR (2.106, 95% CI 1.729–2.565), edging PGS000602 on the same UKB setting (AUROC 0.698; pseudo-R² 0.0839; OR 2.055). A key limitation is that most models here (including PGS000604 and PGS000796) primarily report full-model discrimination rather than PRS-only metrics, which reduces comparability across publications; additionally, PGS000796 reports very high full-model performance but appears to be a packaged/cross-source score with unclear PRS-only separation, so it is not promoted over the cleaner, internally consistent PRSweb sibling with strong effect-size support.

All listed candidates are direct matches for testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (e.g., “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Incident testicular cancer”) and broadly comparable basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array/batch), so the decision hinges on the strongest mutually consistent performance evidence without relying on full-model AUROC alone. Within the coherent Cancer PRSweb family (PGS000595–PGS000604), PGS000604 shows the best supported validation performance package among siblings with similar endpoint/covariates: highest reported AUROC (~0.703 with tight CI), highest Nagelkerke R² (~0.0882), and strong per-SD effect size (OR ~2.11), all in European evaluation. Limitation: all PRSweb candidates report only full-model metrics (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), so absolute PRS-only ranking remains uncertain; additionally, other direct-match non-PRSweb candidates (e.g., PGS000796, PGS001164) report very high full-model metrics but come from different study archetypes and/or unclear PRS-only comparability (and PGS000796’s reported R² appears unusually high), so they do not cleanly overturn the within-family evidence advantage of PGS000604.

All 12 candidates are direct matches to testicular carcinoma/testis cancer by trait/efo/phenotyping fields. Within the coherent Cancer PRSweb sibling set (PGS000595–PGS000604) that shares essentially identical endpoint wording and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array/batch), PGS000604 shows the strongest reported validation package (full-model AUROC 0.703 with CI 0.659–0.745; highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² 0.0882; strong per-SD OR 2.106 [1.729–2.565]) and uses a non-trivial SNP set (44 variants) trained/validated in UKB with larger sample sizes than the MGI-based siblings. Although PGS000796 and PGS001164 report higher full-model AUROC, PGS000796’s very high R²/full-model metrics are not clearly PRS-only and come from a cross-cancer risk-prediction context, and PGS001164 is a pan-trait sparse UKB framework model (snpnet) that domain guidance downranks when disease-focused direct-match alternatives exist; additionally, its PRS-only AUROC is modest (0.6296). Main limitation: across the PRSweb siblings, metrics are largely full-model (not PRS-only), so selection relies on within-family comparability and effect sizes rather than clean PRS-only discrimination.

All 12 visible candidates are direct matches for testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer by trait fields and phenotyping (mostly “Malignant neoplasm of testis”; one explicitly “Incident testicular cancer”). Within the coherent Cancer PRSweb family (PGS000595–PGS000604) with comparable basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, batch/array) and consistent EUR ancestry, PGS000604 is best supported by the strongest reported discrimination/effect-size package: full-model AUROC 0.703 (0.659–0.745) with the highest per-SD OR (2.106; 1.729–2.565) and highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0882) among those siblings. The main limitation is that these are full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), and another direct-match framework score (PGS001164, snpnet) reports explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework which domain knowledge flags as often underperforming in external generalization; thus confidence is reduced to Moderate rather than High.

All 11 candidates are direct concept matches at the trait_reported/trait_efo level, but endpoint fidelity differs: several models target progression/dementia (PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777) rather than PD risk/status, making them weaker for the generic target. Among the PD status models, PGS000903 (Lancet Neurol meta-analysis) has strong structural support (C+T with 1,805 variants vs mostly very sparse GWAS-hit scores) and the strongest visible PD-risk discrimination signals in this pool (full-model AUROC 0.692; reported R² 0.054; OR 6.25 for top vs bottom quartile), with clean/basic covariates (PCs, age, sex) and a coherent multi-cohort disease-focused development/validation context. However, confidence is limited because the key reported metrics appear to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), making cross-model comparability imperfect; several other candidates report full-model AUROCs as well (e.g., PGS001774 AUROC 0.8) but with heavier non-genetic risk-factor packaging (including family history and multiple epidemiologic variables), which reduces interpretability for standalone PRS ranking.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (Parkinson disease), but several are endpoint-mismatched toward progression/dementia (PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777), making them less suitable for the generic target trait. Among the models with phenotyping_reported explicitly "Parkinson's disease", PGS000903 (Lancet Neurol meta-analysis) has the strongest visible PRS-relevant evidence package: a substantially larger variant count (1805) than other GWAS-hit scores and explicit effect-size support (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25 [4.26–9.28]) plus a reported R²=0.054 (not labeled PRS-only, but still supportive) and full-model AUROC=0.692, with relatively clean basic covariates (PCs(1-5), age, sex). However, confidence is limited because no candidate provides clearly identified PGS-only AUROC/R², and full-model AUROC values are not directly comparable across differing covariate sets (e.g., PGS001774’s AUROC=0.8 likely reflects heavier non-genetic covariates; PGS000750 includes family history), preventing a clearly high-quality single winner.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (Parkinson disease), but several have endpoint mismatches for the generic target (e.g., cognitive/motor progression: PGS000056, PGS000211; Parkinson’s disease dementia: PGS000777) or comparatively heavy non-genetic packaging (e.g., family history and singleton LoF count in PGS000750; broad risk-factor bundle including family history/BMI/smoking in PGS001774; environmental exposure covariates in PGS004924). Among the models with a straightforward Parkinson’s disease endpoint and relatively basic covariates (PCs/age/sex), the 2021 Lancet Neurology pair (PGS000902/PGS000903) forms the strongest coherent disease-focused family in the provided context. Between them, PGS000903 is better supported by the visible performance evidence (reports full-model AUROC=0.692 and R²=0.054 plus OR top vs bottom quartile=6.25) and has a much larger variant set (1,805) than the GWAS-hits-only sibling PGS000902 (90 variants; AUROC=0.651). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), so cross-model comparability and PRS-only strength cannot be confirmed from this context, keeping the recommendation below high-confidence.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_reported/trait_efo are Parkinson disease), but several are endpoint-shifted to progression/dementia (PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777) or include heavier non-genetic packaging (e.g., family history and other risk factors in PGS001774; family history plus LoF burden in PGS000750; environmental exposure terms in PGS004924), which reduces comparability for selecting a standalone PD PRS. Among the candidates with a clean PD diagnosis endpoint and relatively basic covariates (PCs/age/sex), the two Lancet Neurology scores (PGS000902 and PGS000903) form the strongest coherent disease-focused study family; within that family, PGS000903 is better supported by the visible metrics (higher reported full-model AUROC 0.692 and an OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25, plus an R² field reported) than PGS000902 (full-model AUROC 0.651, no additional effect-size metrics shown). However, the evidence remains limited because the AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and covariate differences across models make cross-score AUROC comparisons non-equivalent; thus the selection is best-available but not high-certainty.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_reported/trait_efo align to Parkinson disease), but several have endpoint mismatches (e.g., progression/cognitive decline: PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777) rather than generic PD risk/status. Among the models with phenotyping_reported = Parkinson's disease, PGS000903 (Lancet Neurol 2021) is best supported by a combination of (i) endpoint fidelity (PD diagnosis), (ii) stronger structural properties than GWAS-hits-only scores (C+T with 1,805 variants vs <100-variant scores), and (iii) the most directly supportive PRS-relevant evidence available in this context (reported full_model_r2=0.054 and a strong OR=6.25 for top vs bottom quartile), while using only basic covariates (PCs, age, sex). Limitation: no candidate reports clearly isolated PRS-only AUROC/R2, and the available AUROC/C-index values are largely full-model and not directly comparable across differing covariate sets (e.g., PGS001774 includes multiple non-genetic risk factors and reports AUROC=0.8, likely not PRS-only), so the choice remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease).
